text:
maria_gomez: Hey — running into a weird SDK issue on Android: using Retrofit service that returns a kotlinx.coroutines Flow, and one logical operation ends up triggering the network call twice which then triggers duplicate token refreshes (we see double 401->refresh->retry loops). Repro attached below.
maria_gomez: Repro snippet:
```
interface ApiService {
  @GET("/events")
  fun streamEvents(): Flow<Event>
}

// usage
viewModelScope.launch {
  api.streamEvents()
    .map { /* map to UI */ }
    .collect { /* render */ }
}
```

maria_gomez: Logs:
```
D/OkHttp: --> GET /events
D/Auth: 401 received, refreshing token
D/OkHttp: --> GET /events
D/Auth: 401 received, refreshing token
```

maria_gomez: We're not calling collect twice explicitly. Happens intermittently after background/foreground and on cold start sometimes. Anyone seen Flow + Retrofit produce duplicate calls like this?

sam_kim: Is the Flow cold? Each collect will trigger a new call, but if you only collect once that shouldn't happen. Which CallAdapterFactory are you using? Retrofit's built-in or kotlinx-coroutines adapter?

maria_gomez: Using `retrofit2-kotlinx-coroutines-adapter` (the Flow adapter in our SDK wrapper). Single collect. Also happens when we `.buffer()` the flow downstream.

jess_price: Could be a retry behavior: OkHttp's `RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor` can re-run the request on connection failures, but 401 flows shouldn't cause two parallel attempts unless the original call is duplicated by the adapter.

ali_chen: Two quick possibilities:
- Flow is being re-subscribed because something upstream re-triggers collection (lifecycle weirdness)
- The CallAdapter is creating two underlying calls for a single Flow subscription (adapter bug)

ali_chen: Can you dump stack traces for both HTTP calls? They should have distinct call IDs, body/headers. Also does the request body implement one-shot streaming (can't be replayed)?

maria_gomez: Posted call-ids and stack fragments. Both show the same call path but different OkHttp call objects. Looks like adapter is creating two calls.

ron_rivers: Another angle — auth refresh concurrency. Our AuthInterceptor refreshes token when it sees 401 and then retries. If two calls concurrently hit 401 they can both race to refresh and both update token store -> duplicate refreshes and waste quotas.

ron_rivers: Short-term workaround: make token refresh guarded by a Mutex so only one coroutine performs refresh; others wait for the new token.

ron_rivers: Example (in SDK auth layer):
```
private val refreshMutex = Mutex()
suspend fun getValidToken(): String {
  if (needsRefresh()) {
    refreshMutex.withLock {
      if (needsRefresh()) {
        refreshToken() // network call
      }
    }
  }
  return tokenStore.current()
}
```

maria_gomez: That helped reduce duplicates in local testing. But still curious: why are there two underlying calls for one collect? That feels like a bug in our Flow CallAdapter.

sam_kim: Can you share which adapter impl? If it's third-party or our wrapper we should inspect how it creates the Call and maps it to Flow. A common pattern uses `callbackFlow` which needs careful cancellation handling; if cancellation + re-subscription race, the adapter might start a second call before first fully cancelled.

maria_gomez: Adapter code uses `callbackFlow` and `call.enqueue(...)` + `awaitClose { call.cancel() }`. I wonder if `awaitClose` isn't yet invoked when upstream triggers a new collect because lifecycle hasn't fully torn down previous coroutine.

jess_price: If `callbackFlow` is used, make sure to wrap the retrofit Call in `call.clone()` for each enqueue. And ensure `awaitClose` reliably cancels. Another defensive fix: mark the Flow as `shareIn(scope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(...), replay = 1)` at the SDK surface for single-shared consumers.

ali_chen: Agree. But making SDK do `shareIn` changes behavior for callers; better to fix adapter to be more explicit and not create multiple enqueues per subscription. Also add a test that uses a TestCoroutineScope to simulate rapid cancel/resubscribe.

maria_gomez: I'll try replacing `callbackFlow` with a `suspendCancellableCoroutine` wrapper that does a single call per collect. Example attempt:
```
suspend fun <T> Call.awaitResponseSuspend(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object: Callback<T> { ... onResponse { cont.resume(response) } ... })
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
}
```

sam_kim: That approach can be fine for single-shot flows. For streaming endpoints you need to keep callbackFlow. But for our events endpoint it is long-lived; maybe it's better to return a cold flow that wraps a single WebSocket-like stream.

ron_rivers: Also add a guard in Auth layer so refresh only happens once across instances: `synchronized refresh token tokenRefreshInProgress` or the Mutex impl is best.

maria_gomez: Filing a bug and PR plan:
- Create issue describing duplicate-enqueue in flow adapter + logs (DEVEX-1192)
- Add integration test simulating cancel/resubscribe on emulator (API 29+)
- Implement Mutex-based token refresh in AuthInterceptor as interim (small PR)
- Fix adapter to ensure one Call per collect and use `call.clone()` defensively

maria_gomez: @sam_kim can you take ownership of the adapter fix? I'll do the token mutex PR today.

sam_kim: Yup I'll take the adapter. I'll also add a `--flaky` emulator test to the CI to reproduce lifecycle churn.

ci-bot: Created issue DEVEX-1192 and linked to pipeline test job #3781.

jess_price: Nice. For the PR description include how this interacts with `retryOnConnectionFailure` and call.clone() semantics. Also mention downstream impact: duplicate events and doubled telemetry/events count.

ali_chen: Once PRs are up add a short note in the Android SDK migration guide: "If you used Flow adapter X, upgrade to version Y to avoid duplicate enqueues and auth races." Keep it small.

maria_gomez: Thanks all — will push the mutex PR and link to DEVEX-1192. If you see anything else to try please ping here. :thumbsup:
